rows.activity_label: Automated test generation and test automation

rows.item: Post-launch hypercare (two weeks)
Post-launch hypercare (two weeks)
Post-launch hypercare (two weeks)

E1.item: Discovery workshops, backlog and acceptance criteria
E1.move_up: Writing down the distributor's current order, approval and QuickBooks routines before the workshops would turn more of this into drafting.

E2.item: QuickBooks Online technical spike and data audit of the distributor's company file
E2.move_up: Read-only API access to a copy of the real QuickBooks company file before kickoff would turn most of the audit into scripted queries.

E3.item: Architecture and data model design (tenancy, roles, orders, invoices, payments, sync mapping)
E3.move_up: Agreeing field ownership per synced entity before the design session would make the model checkable against written rules.

E4.item: User flows and wireframes for the customer portal and the back office
E4.move_up: Starting from an existing B2B portal pattern library and the written acceptance criteria would let AI draft more of the flows.

E5.item: Visual design and responsive design system
E5.move_up: Adopting an off-the-shelf design system and theming it, instead of designing one, would move this up.

E6.item: Repository, CI/CD pipeline, agent instructions and test commands

E7.item: Environments and infrastructure as code (dev, staging, production, managed Postgres, secrets, backups)

E9.item: Audit log, error monitoring and structured logging

E10.item: UI component library and responsive app shell

E11.item: Sign-in, password reset and session management
caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E11.move_up: Using the auth provider's hosted sign-in pages would leave less security code for the agent to write.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E12.move_up: A written invite-token spec (expiry, single use, rate limits) would let the agent work against tests instead of review.

E13.item: Role-based access control and tenant isolation
caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E13.move_up: A permission matrix written as test fixtures before coding would make every authorization change machine-checked.

E14.move_up: Settling the approval edge cases (limit changes, approver absent, multiple approvers) in writing before the build would move this up.

E15.item: Company admin user management (users, roles, approval limit, deactivation)
caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E15.move_up: Reusing the authorization layer from E13 unchanged keeps this to screens and tests.

E16.item: Product catalog with customer prices and stock
E16.move_up: Knowing where customer prices live (the first open question) would remove the main ambiguity.

E18.item: Order history with search and filters

E20.item: Email notifications (invites, approvals, order confirmations, payment receipts)

E22.item: Card payment of one or several invoices through Stripe
caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E22.move_up: A Stripe test-mode account with webhook fixtures and recorded multi-invoice scenarios from day one would move this up the band.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E23.move_up: Replaying recorded Stripe event sequences (out-of-order, duplicate, failed) in CI would make the webhook handler fully machine-checked.

E24.item: QuickBooks OAuth connection, token rotation and production app approval
caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E24.move_up: Starting the Intuit production-key review in week one and keeping token handling in a small, tested module would move this up.

E25.item: Sync engine: job queue, change data capture and webhooks, idempotency, rate limits, retries, sync log
E25.move_up: A recorded QuickBooks sandbox harness that simulates throttling and missed webhooks would give the agent a pass/fail check.

E26.item: Customer mapping and two-way customer sync
E26.move_up: A cleaned export of the real customer list with the distributor's matching rules written down would move this up.

E27.item: Products, prices and stock sync from QuickBooks
E27.move_up: Confirming where prices and stock live would turn this into a mapping exercise against a known API.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E28.move_up: A sandbox company configured with the distributor's real tax and terms setup would let tests check invoice output end to end.

E29.item: Invoices and payments from QuickBooks to the portal
E29.move_up: Recorded change-data-capture payloads for edits, voids and credit memos would make this testable offline.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E30.move_up: An hour with the distributor's bookkeeper to write down the deposit and fee entries would remove the tacit-knowledge block.

E31.move_up: Written field-ownership rules per entity would shrink the conflict cases and make each one a test.

E32.move_up: Agreed mismatch tolerances written as test cases would make the report checkable.

E33.item: Initial data load and customer onboarding
E33.move_up: A copy of the production company file for repeated dry runs, with validation counts as checks, would move this up.

E34.item: Back office shell and staff roles
caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E34.move_up: Reusing the customer authorization layer for staff roles instead of a second one would cut the security-sensitive code.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)

E39.item: Integration test suite against the QuickBooks sandbox and Stripe test mode
E39.move_up: Stable sandbox fixtures and recorded third-party responses would cut the flaky-test triage.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E40.move_up: Scanner and authorization-test gates in CI from week one would leave fewer findings for the final review.

E43.item: User acceptance testing support and feedback rework round
E43.move_up: Turning each piece of UAT feedback into a failing test before fixing it would move the rework up the band.

caps: G2 high stakes (auth, payments, personal data, compliance or irreversible changes)
E44.move_up: A rehearsed cutover on staging with the same scripts and checklists would make most steps repeatable and checkable.

E45.move_up: Keeping decision records and runbooks current during the build leaves only the walkthrough for the end.

E46.move_up: Production logs and alerts wired to reproducible test cases would turn more incidents into reproducible bugs.
